claims.text: Studies of interventions to change diet-related behaviours comprise 70.2% of the identified choice architecture micro-environment evidence base.
Studies of interventions relating to physical activity account for 19.1% of the identified evidence base.
Studies of interventions relating to alcohol consumption account for 7.3% of the identified evidence base.
Studies of interventions relating to tobacco use account for 3.4% of the identified evidence base.
Interventions involving point-of-choice labelling and prompting together account for over 40% of the identified study reports.

Choice architecture interventions within micro-environments can be grouped into nine types that aggregate into two higher-level classes: altering properties and altering placement of objects or stimuli.

evidence.description: This evidence base is dominated by studies of interventions to change diet-related behaviours such as food purchasing and consumption (70.2% of study reports).
Reported distribution showed 'many fewer studies relating to physical activity (19.1%)'.
Identified study reports for alcohol accounted for 7.3% of the evidence base.
Identified study reports for tobacco use accounted for 3.4% of the evidence base.
The two types of intervention most frequently encountered, together accounting for over 40% of study reports, were those involving point-of-choice labelling, and prompting.

We grouped the available evidence that was consistent with our definition into nine types... aggregated into two higher-level classes of intervention: i. those that involve altering the properties of objects or stimuli within a micro-environment, and ii. those that involve altering their placement.

methodologies.name: Iterative configurative scoping review using text mining
methodologies.description: A systematic, iterative, and configurative scoping review employing text mining technologies to map empirical evidence of micro-environmental choice architecture interventions across four health behaviour domains.
conditions: Interventions altering properties or placement of objects or stimuli in micro-environments
Targeting diet, physical activity, alcohol, or tobacco use

limitations.text: Formal critical appraisal and synthesis to estimate the direction and magnitude of effects reported in included studies was beyond the scope of this work.
Data on the long-term durability of behavioural effects of interventions were not systematically extracted.
The proposed definition and typology are provisional and primarily descriptive.
Prior work lacked clear definitional and conceptual clarity concerning applications of choice architecture to public health intervention.

future_work.text: Conduct rigorous primary research and systematic reviews to estimate the direction, magnitude, and moderators of choice architecture intervention effects.
Investigate the cumulative effects of repeated exposure to micro-environment alterations over time within long-term evaluative frameworks.
Explore implementation issues including public acceptability, financial impacts, and the necessity of regulatory or legislative frameworks.
